transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?
Ever since my friend was killed, I’ve had this constant mix of guilt, fear, and anger. I thought it would ease with time, but it hasn’t. That’s why I’m here.
How long ago did your friend pass away?
About two years and three months ago. It was on that walking tour.
Since your friend's death, have you experienced intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares that make you feel like you're re-living what happened?

Yes. A crosswalk signal, the sound of a truck growling, even seeing a walking-tour map—it can all suddenly bring the whole scene back. I see my friend stepping off the curb so clearly, before I can stop it.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or conversations—like walking tours, crosswalks, or talking about your friend—because they bring up these memories?

Yes. I go out of my way to avoid that intersection. And I’ve stopped signing up for most tours or safety meetings, because the conversations always seem to circle back to what happened there, and I just can’t bear it.
Since the incident, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually on edge, easily startled, or constantly watching out for danger, even in situations that used to feel safe?
Yes. When I’m near traffic, I watch every truck, every curb, and the people crossing. It feels like I have to catch something dangerous before it happens again.
